- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 5–10 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 1–3% lag correction to forecast.
- For 30d horizon, if model is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is volatile, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to pivot; adjust forecast mid-horizon by +1–2% to align with sentiment reversal.
